about: Every BoardDetect.DetectBoard call in the C# test class, in file order, with its inputs as written there. DetectBoardTestMany makes six calls and each is its own case here, numbered from 0; the seventh, 'PX4 BL FMU v1.x' at lines 35-44, is commented out in the C# and is not a case.
Each call passes port "com1" and a list of DeviceInfo (ExtLibs/ArduPilot/DeviceInfo.cs). 'devices' is that list, field for field.
'csharp_asserts' is what the test checks: {"equals": board} for 'if (ans != X) Assert.Fail()', {"not": "none"} for 'if (ans == none) Assert.Fail()', null for a call whose result is not checked.

'device_rules' is what BoardDetect.cs:66-197 (the device list) concludes: {"board": b} or {"board": "chbootloader", "chbootloader": name}, {"probe": "fmu_v2_or_v3"} for the replug prompt at :148, or "no_match" to go on to WMI.

Where the device list does not decide, the C# reads the live Win32_SerialPort table (BoardDetect.cs:199), not the list the test passed. 'serial_ports' is the row Windows lists for the same device on com1 - its hardware id, the '\0' instance suffix BoardDetect.cs:134 shows, and a Name ending '(COM1)' - and 'serial_port_rules' is what BoardDetect.cs:212-367 concludes from it.

'csharp_result' is what the C# test gets from BoardDetect.cs as it stands, read from the source: "passes", "fails", "machine-dependent" or "unchecked", with 'why'. In the test process CustomMessageBox.ShowEvent is never set, so every CustomMessageBox.Show throws 'ShowEvent Not Set' (ExtLibs/Utilities/CustomMessageBox.cs:40-43); the replug prompt at BoardDetect.cs:150 throws into the catch at :194, and the question at :412-413 throws out of DetectBoard.

cases.why: 0483:5740 is a new-style id (BoardDetect.cs:82) and 'fmuv2' is px4v2 (:87-91).

'PX4 BL FMU v2.x' is no board string the list rules know, so the C# reads the test machine's own Win32_SerialPort table. With this device on it, 26AC:0011 is the 'chibios or normal px4' rule (:242-291), whose replug prompt at :246 throws out of DetectBoard; with no known id on it, the question at :412-413 throws. It passes only on a machine with some other recognised board attached.
As DetectBoardTestMany[0]: the same id, and the list rules do not know 'PX4 BL FMU v3.x'.

The list rules know 'PX4 FMU v4.x', not 'PX4 BL FMU v4.x'. From WMI, 26AC:0012 is px4v4 (:297-301), which passes - but only if the device is on the test machine, and the method has already thrown at DetectBoardTestMany[0] unless it is.
From WMI, 26AC:0013 is px4v4pro (:302-306); the list rules do not know the product string.
From WMI, 26AC:0032 is a ChibiOS bootloader named CUAVv5 (:231-240); the list rules know 'PX4 FMU v5.x', not 'PX4 BL FMU v5.x'.
VID_2DAE is a new-style id (:83). The product string has ' BL', not '-BL', so nothing is stripped from the name (:128).
1209:5740 is a new-style id (:85) and 'fmuv2-bl' lower-cased is px4v2 (:87).
VID_2DAE is a new-style id (:83) and 'CubeBlack' is not fmuv2/3/4, so it is a ChibiOS bootloader named CubeBlack (:128-129).

The second device's 'PX4 FMU v2.x' reaches the replug prompt (:148-150). In the test process that throws into the catch at :194, and the question at :412-413 then throws out of DetectBoard. In the application the probe returns px4v3, px4v2 or none (:169-189). No path in DetectBoard returns chbootloader for 2341:0010.
As DetectBoardTest3: 'PX4 FMU v2.x' is the replug prompt, whatever the id. From WMI 26AC:0010 would be px4 (:222-230), not chbootloader, but the list decides first.
The second device's 'PX4 FMU v5.x' is fmuv5 (:132-137), returned before WMI is read. The chbootloader the test expects is the WMI rule for 26AC:0032 (:231-240), which the list rule pre-empts.
'PX4 FMU v3.x' is the replug prompt (:148), as in DetectBoardTest3.
0483:5740 is a new-style id (:82); an empty product string is no known board, so it is a ChibiOS bootloader with an empty name (:128-129).
'PX4 FMU v2.x' is the replug prompt (:148), as in DetectBoardTest3. The description is never read.
1209:5740 is a new-style id (:85), and as DetectBoardTest7.
